title: Stop Buying Canned Cranberry Sauce: This 3-Ingredient Homemade Version Takes 10 Minutes
description: Skip the canned jelly this Thanksgiving. Make this ridiculously easy 3-ingredient homemade cranberry sauce in just 10 minutes with zero cleanup hassle.
story: Look, I love taking shortcuts in the kitchen as much as the next tired apartment dweller, but the canned cranberry jelly that slides out with the metal clunk lines? Hard pass. Last year, I got desperate and threw together what was left in my fridge—a bag of fresh cranberries from Trader Joe's, some organic orange juice, and pure cane sugar. Honestly, I didn't expect much. But standing there in my tiny kitchen, listening to those berries pop and release that bright, zesty aroma, I knew I was never going back. The first time I tested this, I cranked the heat too high and turned my stovetop into a sticky red crime scene—keep it at a medium simmer so you don't burn the sugar! It takes literally one saucepan, meaning I don't have to spend my evening scrubbing baked-on gunk when I'd rather be horizontal on the couch.
ingredients: 12 ounces fresh cranberries, rinsed and picked through (Aldi or Trader Joe's bags work great)
3/4 cup organic granulated sugar (adjust down to 1/2 cup if you prefer it tart)
1/2 cup fresh orange juice (plus 1 teaspoon of orange zest if you want extra pop)
A tiny pinch of kosher salt to balance the sweetness
instructions: Step 1: Dump your rinsed cranberries, sugar, orange juice, water, and a tiny pinch of kosher salt straight into a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Step 2: Give it a quick stir and let it come to a gentle bubble. You'll start hearing the berries pop open—that's totally normal and kind of satisfying.

Step 3: Turn the heat down to medium-low. Let it simmer for about 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally with a wooden spoon until most of the berries have burst and the liquid thickens up into a glossy jam.
Step 4: Take it off the heat and let it cool completely. It thickens up even more as it sits in the fridge, I promise!
proHack: Don't panic if it looks a bit too runny when you take it off the heat. Pectin naturally activates as it cools down, so give it an hour in the fridge and it'll reach that perfect spreadable jam texture.
storage: Store your leftover homemade cranberry sauce in a tightly sealed mason jar or glass container in the fridge for up to 10 days. It also freezes amazingly well for up to 3 months—just thaw it overnight in the fridge before serving.

faqs.question: Can I substitute bottled orange juice for fresh?
faqs.answer: You can, but fresh squeezed orange juice gives it a much brighter, less sugary taste. If using store-bought bottled juice, try to grab one without added pulp and check the sugar levels so it doesn't turn out overly sweet.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the sauce from tasting too bitter?
faqs.answer: Cranberries are naturally tart and contain plenty of natural bitterness in their skins. Make sure you don't skip the sugar, and if you use orange zest, make sure you only grate the bright orange outer skin—avoid the bitter white pith underneath!
